Herb
ĕrb
n. (a seed-bearing plant; the original food of man and beast; rendering Hebrew eseb, yaraq, Greek lachanon)
From Latin herba, grass, green growth. In Genesis the herb is a category of creation, defined by a single property: it bears seed.

Biblical Definition

Herb is a creation category before it is a kitchen one, and its defining mark is reproduction: “Let the earth bring forth grass, the herb yielding seed, and the fruit tree yielding fruit after his kind, whose seed is in itself” (Gen 1:11). Two things are established there and never revoked: creatures reproduce after their kind, and the herb carries its own future inside it. God then assigns it as food — “I have given you every herb bearing seed… to you it shall be for meat” (Gen 1:29) — and to the beasts as well, “every green herb for meat” (Gen 1:30). The original diet of man and animal alike is vegetable, and flesh is granted only after the flood: “even as the green herb have I given you all things” (Gen 9:3). Between the two stands the curse, which puts labour into the arrangement: “Thorns also and thistles shall it bring forth to thee; and thou shalt eat the herb of the field” (Gen 3:18).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines an herb as a plant or vegetable with a soft or succulent stalk or stem, which dies to the root every year — distinguished from a tree or shrub by its perishing stem.

expand to see more

HERB, n. erb. A plant or vegetable with a soft or succulent stalk or stem, which dies to the root every year, and is thus distinguished from a tree and a shrub.

2. In the Linnean botany, that part of a vegetable which springs from the root and is terminated by the fructification.

3. Grass; herbage.

God said, let the earth bring forth grass, the herb yielding seed. Gen. i.

Key Scripture

Gen 1:11 — "And God said, Let the earth bring forth grass, the herb yielding seed, and the fruit tree yielding fruit after his kind, whose seed is in itself, upon the earth: and it was so."

Gen 1:29 — "And God said, Behold, I have given you every herb bearing seed, which is upon the face of all the earth, and every tree, in the which is the fruit of a tree yielding seed; to you it shall be for meat."

Gen 9:3 — "Every moving thing that liveth shall be meat for you; even as the green herb have I given you all things."

Gen 3:18 — "Thorns also and thistles shall it bring forth to thee; and thou shalt eat the herb of the field;"

Modern Corruption

After his kind quietly abandoned, and the herb's self-contained seed treated as an accident — while diet is moralized into a religion with clean and unclean of its own devising.

expand to see more

Genesis 1:11 says twice what modern origins accounts deny: things reproduce after their kind, and the seed is in itself. The dictionary holds the six-day creation of Genesis as its standard, and it holds it here at the level of the herb, because the phrase is repeated at every stage of the account rather than mentioned once. Whatever variation occurs within kinds — and it plainly occurs — the text asserts fixed kinds each carrying its own seed, and the assertion is structural to the chapter.

The second drift is dietary moralism. Genesis grants the herb, then grants flesh after the flood, and the New Testament forecloses the argument entirely: the kingdom of God is not meat and drink, and he that eateth is not to despise him that eateth not. Where eating becomes a system of purity and defilement of a person's own devising, Romans 14 is being violated in both directions — and Paul, notably, calls the man who eateth herbs the weaker brother, and then commands the stronger not to despise him.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew eseb (H6212), herb, green plant — the seed-bearing category of Gen 1:11; yaraq (H3419), green things, garden herbs; Greek lachanon (G3001), a garden herb, potherb.

expand to see more

Hebrew eseb (H6212) — herb, herbage; the seed-yielding creation category and the food of Gen 1:29-30.

Hebrew yaraq (H3419) — green, herbs; better is a dinner of herbs where love is, than a stalled ox and hatred therewith (Pro 15:17).

Greek lachanon (G3001) — a garden herb; the mustard seed becoming the greatest among herbs (Mat 13:32).

Usage

"“The herb yielding seed… whose seed is in itself” — each kind carries its own future."

"“I have given you every herb bearing seed… for meat” — the original diet."

"“Thou shalt eat the herb of the field” — the same food, now with thorns in the way."
